text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended lower in dull trading with players seen rolling out their July positions ahead of the first notice day on Tuesday. The July/September spread widened to $15 at the close from $6 at Thursday's close. September finished $16 lower at $1,785 per tonne, while July gave up $11 to close at $1,770 per tonne. Warm weather in Brazil continued to undermine sentiment.

Arabica futures in New York ended mixed in sluggish trading. The market attempted to rebound from Thursday's sharp sell off but ran into a late-session bout of local selling. July lost 35 points to close at 189.90 cents/lb. By contrast September added 3.20 cents/lb to close at 169.30 cents/lb. Continued mild weather in top-grower Brazil and talk of a build up in stocks pending CSCE certification weighed on the market. Some Brazilian meteorologists said the recent wave of warm weather in the country's coffee growing regions may be due to the El Nino, which they said could have some unwelcome, rainy implications. Brazil's coffee region saw unseasonal rains this month which have delayed the harvest and impacted the quality of the beans. They also noted the occurrence of early scattered flowerings (the first stage in the development of next year's harvest) which normally begin at the end of August, beginning of September. USDA - On Friday, the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) released coffee production, supply and distribution balances - based on the production data released on June 13 - in its bulletin Tropical Products: World Markets and Trade. The USDA estimated 1997/98 world coffee exports at 84.4 million 60-kg bags, up from a revised 82.9 million bags seen in 1996/97. The 1996/97 figure seems to be overly generous and compares to our recent estimate of 77.9 million bags. USDA previously pegged 1996/97 world coffee exports at 79.6 million bags. USDA said total coffee supply in producing countries in 1997/98 is forecast at 130.5 million bags, down 2.5 per cent from the prior year largely due to lower beginning stock levels. The Department estimated beginning stocks in producer countries in 1997/98 at 26.0 million bags, the lowest level since 1980/81 and down 6.1 million bags from 1996/97. USDA pegged the decline on the significant increase in exports. It forecast 1997/98 ending stocks in producer countries at 20.0 million bags. Earlier

INDIA - According to trade sources coffee production in 1997/98 (October/September) is expected to top 3.8 million bags, up from this season's 3.0 million bags. The new crop estimate is based on the blossoming of the 1997/98 crop, which received good rain in March. For coffee, pre-blossom March/April showers are critical.
UNITED STATES - CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 280 60-kg bags as of June 26, to 45,893 bags. However, there were 14,594 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

UNITED STATES - Coffee roastings for the week ended June 21 totalled approximately 290,000 60-kg bags, down from 310,000 bags in the previous week and compared with 305,000 bags in the corresponding week one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 8.345 million bags, versus 8.115 million bags the same year ago period.

PHILIPPINES ** - The Philippines exported 66,200 bags of coffee in January/March 1997, up from 46,600 bags the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar year 1996 reached 209,500 bags. The country shipped 11,900 bags of solubles to South Korea in January/March 1997, up from 9,700 bags the same period in 1996. Singapore took 6,800 bags of soluble coffee from the Philippines in January/March 1997 against 6,200 bags the same period in 1996.
